## Circular to Licensed Corporations Providing Online Trading Services

## Reminder of Adequate Information Security Measures to Combat Possible Denial-of-Service Attacks

Some US media have recently reported that terrorists might launch denial-of-service attacks against financial institutions' online stock trading and banking websites. The SFC would like to remind all licensed corporations that provide online trading services of the importance of adequate information security for combating malicious cyber attacks.

Denial-of-service  attack  refers  to  any  attempt  to  prevent  legitimate  users  from  accessing information or services from a server by repeatedly bombarding the server with so many hits or messages that the server shuts down or becomes inaccessible.

Part  IV  of  the  Management,  Supervision  and  Internal  Control  Guidelines  for  Persons Licensed  by  or  Registered  with  the  Securities  and  Futures  Commission  provides  some guidance on information management for the licensed or registered person.  It indicates that a firm  should  establish  policies  and  procedures  to  ensure  the  integrity,  security,  availability, reliability and thoroughness of all information including electronically stored data, relevant to the firm's business operations.

To prepare for possible cyber attacks, it is recommended that management should carefully evaluate  whether  your  firm's  existing  security  measures  are  adequate  for  preventing  and detecting any cyber attack against your online trading facilities.

For  the  avoidance  of  doubt,  a  licensed  corporation  remains  responsible  for  ensuring  the security of its online trading facilities even if it has outsourced this function to an external service provider.

Furthermore,  if  online  trading  service  is  critical  to  the  firm's  entire  operation,  it  is  also important  for  your  firm's  business  continuity  plan  to  take  into  the  account  possible interruption caused by cyber attacks and make available alternative trading arrangements for your clients.

Intermediaries Supervision Department Securities and Futures Commission
